title: Proposte e suggerimenti
intro: Oggi impari a fare proposte, a suggerire alternative e a ragionare insieme su vantaggi e svantaggi per arrivare a una decisione. Impari Let's, Why don't we e How about, e la prima parte della regola più difficile: quando dopo un verbo si usa -ing e quando si usa to più infinito.
goals: Fare una proposta con Let's, Why don't we, How about e Shall we
Descrivere vantaggi e svantaggi di due soluzioni
Scegliere tra gerundio (-ing) e infinito (to) dopo i verbi più comuni
Scrivere una mail con una raccomandazione e una proposta chiara

falseFriends.trap: Dopo suggest non si usa to + infinito: si dice 'I suggest going' o 'I suggest that we go', mai 'I suggest to go'.
Si usa anche al lavoro ed è più formale di suggest: 'We propose a new plan.' Attenzione però: 'to propose to someone' vuol dire chiedere di sposarsi.
Non vuol dire 'conveniente' come economico: per quello si dice cheap o good value. 'Is Monday convenient?' = Lunedì ti va bene?
Si dice 'I prefer coffee to tea' o 'I prefer working to studying'. Non 'I prefer more coffee than tea'.

grammar.title: Proposte (Let's, Why don't we, How about) e gerundio o infinito, parte 1
explainIt: Per fare una proposta usa queste formule. Let's + verbo base: 'Let's meet on Monday.' Why don't we + verbo base: 'Why don't we start with the homepage?' How about + forma in -ing: 'How about starting with the homepage?' What about + -ing: 'What about asking the client?' Shall we + verbo base: 'Shall we begin?' Sono tutte frasi che vanno bene in riunione, in mail e al telefono.

Per rispondere a una proposta: 'Good idea.' 'Sounds good.' 'That works for me.' 'Why not?' Se non sei d'accordo: 'I'm not sure about that.' 'I'd rather not.' 'How about doing it another way?' Puoi anche fare una controproposta: 'What if we do it next week instead?'

Il verbo suggest è molto usato per proporre qualcosa. Ha due forme corrette. Suggest + -ing: 'I suggest meeting on Thursday.' Suggest + that + soggetto + verbo base: 'I suggest that we meet on Thursday.' Non si dice mai 'I suggest to meet'. Lo stesso vale per recommend: 'I recommend using a template.' 'I recommend that you use a template.'

Dopo certi verbi si usa la forma in -ing (gerundio). I più utili: suggest, recommend, consider, avoid, enjoy, finish, mind, keep, postpone, risk, practise. Esempi: 'We considered moving the site.' 'I enjoy working with this team.' 'Do you mind waiting?' 'Please avoid using too many colours.' Anche dopo le preposizioni si usa -ing: before, after, instead of, without, how about, interested in. 'Instead of calling, send an email.'

Dopo altri verbi si usa to + infinito. I più utili: decide, want, need, hope, plan, agree, offer, refuse, promise, manage, expect, would like. Esempi: 'We decided to postpone the launch.' 'I hope to finish today.' 'She offered to help.' 'We need to talk.' Un trucco per ricordarli, che vale spesso ma non sempre: con questi verbi guardi avanti, a qualcosa che vuoi fare. Con i verbi in -ing parli di qualcosa che già fai o consideri. Nella parte due della regola vedrai i verbi che accettano entrambe le forme.
explainEn: To make a suggestion, use these patterns. Let's + base verb: 'Let's meet on Monday.' Why don't we + base verb: 'Why don't we start with the homepage?' How about + -ing form: 'How about starting with the homepage?' What about + -ing: 'What about asking the client?' Shall we + base verb: 'Shall we begin?' They are all fine in meetings, in emails and on the phone.

To answer a suggestion: 'Good idea.' 'Sounds good.' 'That works for me.' 'Why not?' If you are not sure: 'I'm not sure about that.' 'I'd rather not.' 'How about doing it another way?' You can also make a counter-suggestion: 'What if we do it next week instead?'

The verb suggest is very common for proposals. It has two correct patterns. Suggest + -ing: 'I suggest meeting on Thursday.' Suggest + that + subject + base verb: 'I suggest that we meet on Thursday.' We never say 'I suggest to meet'. It is the same with recommend: 'I recommend using a template.' 'I recommend that you use a template.'

After some verbs we use the -ing form (the gerund). The most useful are suggest, recommend, consider, avoid, enjoy, finish, mind, keep, postpone, risk and practise. For example: 'We considered moving the site.' 'I enjoy working with this team.' 'Do you mind waiting?' 'Please avoid using too many colours.' We also use -ing after prepositions: before, after, instead of, without, how about, interested in. 'Instead of calling, send an email.'

After other verbs we use to + infinitive. The most useful are decide, want, need, hope, plan, agree, offer, refuse, promise, manage, expect and would like. For example: 'We decided to postpone the launch.' 'I hope to finish today.' 'She offered to help.' 'We need to talk.' A trick to remember them, which often works but not always: with these verbs you look forward, to something you want to do. With the -ing verbs you talk about something you already do or are considering. In part two of this rule you will see the verbs that accept both forms.

dialogue.title: Choosing a hosting plan
dialogue.context: Luca e Giulia devono scegliere con il cliente Marco un nuovo piano di hosting per il suo negozio online. Ci sono due alternative: una economica e una più cara.

lines.name: Luca
lines.en: Okay, Marco, we have two options for the hosting. Why don't we go through the pros and cons?
lines.it: Allora Marco, abbiamo due opzioni per l'hosting. Perché non vediamo insieme pro e contro?

lines.name: Luca
lines.en: The first plan is cheaper. The downside is that it's a shared server, so it can be slow when there are many visitors.
lines.it: Il primo piano costa meno. Il lato negativo è che è un server condiviso, quindi può essere lento quando ci sono tanti visitatori.

lines.name: Giulia
lines.en: The second plan is more expensive, but the advantage is that you get a dedicated server and daily backups.
lines.it: Il secondo piano costa di più, ma il vantaggio è che hai un server dedicato e backup giornalieri.

lines.name: Marco
lines.en: How much more expensive is it?

lines.name: Giulia
lines.en: About 20 euros a month. I think it's worth paying for, because your shop is growing.
lines.it: Circa 20 euro al mese. Penso che valga la pena pagarlo, perché il tuo negozio sta crescendo.

lines.name: Marco
lines.en: Hmm. I'd rather not spend too much right now. What about starting with the cheaper plan?
lines.it: Mmm. Preferirei non spendere troppo adesso. Che ne dite di iniziare con il piano più economico?

lines.name: Luca
lines.en: That's possible. How about this: we start with the cheaper one and upgrade if the site gets slow?
lines.it: Si può fare. Che ne dici di questo: iniziamo con quello economico e passiamo all'altro se il sito rallenta?

lines.name: Giulia
lines.en: Yes, it's quite straightforward. We'd only need to move the files, which takes about an hour.
lines.it: Sì, è abbastanza semplice. Basterebbe spostare i file: ci vuole circa un'ora.

lines.name: Marco
lines.en: That sounds reasonable. But what if the site crashes during the sales?
lines.it: Mi sembra ragionevole. Ma se il sito va giù durante i saldi?

lines.name: Luca
lines.en: Good question. I suggest moving to the second plan one week before the sales, just in case.
lines.it: Buona domanda. Suggerisco di passare al secondo piano una settimana prima dei saldi, per sicurezza.

lines.name: Marco
lines.en: Okay, that works for me. Let's go ahead with that.
lines.it: D'accordo, per me va bene. Andiamo avanti così.

lines.name: Giulia
lines.en: Great. Shall we agree on the next steps? I'll send you a short proposal by tomorrow.
lines.it: Bene. Ci accordiamo sui prossimi passi? Ti mando una breve proposta entro domani.

writing.taskIt: Un cliente deve scegliere tra due soluzioni per il suo nuovo sito: un modello già pronto (veloce ed economico, meno personalizzabile) oppure un design su misura (più caro, più lungo, ma unico). Scrivi una mail di raccomandazione. Descrivi vantaggi e svantaggi di ciascuna opzione, di' quale consigli e perché (usa 'I recommend' o 'I suggest' con la forma in -ing), proponi il passo successivo con 'Shall we' o 'How about' e chiudi in modo gentile.
writing.taskEn: A client has to choose between two solutions for their new website: a ready-made template (fast and cheap, less flexible) or a custom design (more expensive, longer, but unique). Write a recommendation email. Describe the advantages and disadvantages of each option, say which one you recommend and why (use 'I recommend' or 'I suggest' with the -ing form), suggest the next step with 'Shall we' or 'How about', and close politely.
writing.model:
Subject: Template or custom design? Our recommendation

Dear Marco,

Thank you for your patience. Here is a short comparison of the two options.

Option 1: ready-made template. The main advantage is the cost: it is cheaper, and we can launch in about three weeks. The downside is that it is less flexible, so some pages will look similar to other websites.

Option 2: custom design. The advantage is that your site will be unique and built exactly for your customers. The drawback is the price, and it takes about three months.

Because you want to open the shop before the summer, I recommend starting with the template. We can improve it later, and if the shop grows, we can think about a custom design next year.

How about a short call on Thursday to agree on the next steps? I can also send you a detailed proposal if you like.

Best regards,
Luca
